Surface wave can reach beyond the horizon to some extent. With sky wave propagation it is possible to exploit the ionospheric reflection and thus achieve communication distances up to thousands of kilometers. Near vertical incidence skywave (NVIS) enables skip-zone free communications up to hundreds of kilometers. Due the chaotic and ever-changing nature of the ionosphere and the unstable usability of the HF frequencies in general, a high level of adaptivity in the data modem and in the automatic frequency selection or automatic link establishment (ALE) is critical in the HF radio system. This is especially important in tactical communications where fast and reliable message delivery is crucial. A system that offers only static data waveform modes and fixed frequency or slow ALE is therefore not an option in Finnish Defence Forces tactical operating environment.
